registration.summary: BRTA's statutory registration fee is only two slabs: up to 100cc = Tk 2,000, above 100cc = Tk 3,000 (Road Transport Rules 2022). Electric bikes use the same slabs by motor power: up to 5 kW = Tk 2,000, above 5 kW = Tk 3,000. There is no separate registration slab for 125cc vs 150cc vs 250cc vs 350cc, so all >100cc bikes pay the same BRTA package. The buyer pays on top of ex-showroom price: registration fee + inspection + digital registration certificate (DRC) + RFID retro-reflective number plate + road tax (tax token, 2-year or 10-year) + a one-time Financial Assistance Fund (Trustee Board) fee + 15% VAT on BRTA service fees. Dealers usually collect this as a 'registration package' and may add a service charge.

ev.note: Electric motorcycles and scooters use the same two slabs, set by rated motor power instead of cc: motor up to 5 kW = Tk 2,000 (Sch.1 item 21-ka, same as up to 100cc), above 5 kW = Tk 3,000 (item 21-kha). Every EV listed here is rated 5 kW or less, so it gets the up-to-100cc package. The other package items (inspection, DRC, plate, Trustee fee) are not cc-based; the gazette page read does not cover road tax for EVs, so the up-to-100cc tax token is assumed (confidence medium).

bands.label: ~100cc (up to 100cc)
bands.totalNote: Secondary-source package totals (DeshiBiker, May 2025): 2-year tax token Tk 10,664; 10-year tax token Tk 19,664. PDTS (Jun 2024) lists Tk 10,441 / 19,441 for >90kg ≤100cc and Tk 9,291 / 13,891 for <90kg bikes, so expect roughly Tk 9,300-10,700 (2-yr) or Tk 13,900-19,700 (10-yr).

breakdown.note: Computed as 15% of 2,000+800+540+2,200; official components sum to ~Tk 8,671 (2-yr) and the gap to the ~Tk 10,664 market total is not explained in any source found.

bands.label: ~125cc
bands.totalNote: Same BRTA package as every >100cc bike. DeshiBiker (May 2025): Tk 11,764 (2-yr) / Tk 20,964 (10-yr). PDTS gives Tk 20,764 for 10-yr (likely a typo; 11,764 + 4 x 2,300 = 20,964).

bands.label: ~150-165cc
bands.totalNote: Same as >100cc. Budget reports differ: the Daily Star (4 Jun 2026) said owners of bikes above 150cc would need a TIN; the Dhaka Tribune (6 Jun 2026) said owners of bikes above 165cc would instead show proof of return submission (PSR) at registration and renewal. We could not confirm which rule is in the final Finance Act 2026 (checked 14 Oct 2026), so ask the dealer or BRTA.

bands.label: ~250cc
bands.totalNote: Registration fee schedule has no separate slab above 100cc, so BRTA charges should match the >100cc package. No source found itemising a 250cc registration specifically; dealer packages may differ.

bands.label: ~350cc
bands.totalNote: Same statutory slab as >100cc. Only locally manufactured/assembled bikes up to 375cc are registrable (see ccPolicy). Some brands (e.g. Royal Enfield via IFAD) have run free-2-year-registration promotions. No source itemising a 350cc registration found.

Road tax / tax token, 10 years paid upfront (alternative to 2-year)
Financial Assistance Fund (Trustee Board) one-time fee
VAT 15% on BRTA service fees (registration, inspection, DRC, plate)
above100cc.note: Computed: 15% of 3,000+800+540+2,200. Official components sum to ~Tk 10,971 (2-yr); market quotes are ~Tk 11,764, unexplained Tk ~800 difference may be other charges/rounding.

registration.fitness: Motorcycles do not need a periodic fitness certificate renewal in practice; BRTA issues a fitness certificate with the registration. The gazette's annual fitness fee (Tk 800) applies to non-heavy vehicles generally - confidence low on whether it is charged for private motorcycles.

changes2024to2026.change: Registration fee cut from Tk 4,200 to Tk 2,000 (≤100cc) and Tk 5,600 to Tk 3,000 (>100cc). Codified in Road Transport Rules 2022 Schedule-1.
One-time Financial Assistance Fund (Trustee Board) fee of Tk 1,150 added; owners who registered before 2023 pay it at next tax-token renewal.

source.title: How Much is the Road Tax of a Motorcycle in Bangladesh?

changes2024to2026.change: 10-year tax token rule: a motorcycle's road tax is payable for a maximum of 10 years (upfront ~Tk 11,500 for >100cc, or Tk 2,300 every 2 years). After 10 years the bike gets a 'tax-free' token renewed every 5 years for a token Tk 23 bank deposit.

source.title: What To Do When The Motorcycle Tax Token Validity Exceeds 10 Years?

changes2024to2026.change: Proposed first-ever annual advance income tax (AIT) on motorcycles in the FY2026-27 budget (initially Tk 2,000 for 111-125cc, Tk 5,000 for 126-165cc, Tk 10,000 above 165cc) was dropped after protests. No motorcycle AIT is in force. Budget reports then said owners of bikes above 165cc would show proof of return submission (PSR) at registration and renewal (an earlier report said a TIN for bikes above 150cc); the final Finance Act 2026 text was not confirmed as of 14 Oct 2026.

registration.confidence: medium - statutory fee slabs are confirmed from the gazette; package totals and road-tax amounts come from secondary guides that disagree slightly. BikeBD's itemised table (Oct 2026) still shows pre-2021 registration fees (4,200/5,600), so it was not used for totals.

eligibility.other: Mentally and physically fit; NID required for BSP account

types.feeNote: 1 category (e.g. motorcycle only) Tk 518; 2 categories (e.g. motorcycle + car) Tk 748. Paid online. BikeBD quotes older Tk 345/518 figures - BRTA page is authoritative.
types.validity: Printable immediately from BSP; BRTA advises 2-3 months of practice before the test

types.type: Smart card - professional (needed for commercial riding)
types.extra: Dope test report must be uploaded

documents: Medical certificate from a registered doctor (BRTA form)
Utility bill if current address differs from NID
For smart card: learner licence scanned with pass seal; dope test report (professional only)

exam.notes: Held at the BRTA circle's test centre on the date given on the learner licence. Biometrics taken and fingerprint matched against the NID server before the test. Result uploaded online and sent by SMS within 1 working day. Bring original learner licence and a pen.

steps.title: Create BSP account
steps.detail: Register on bsp.brta.gov.bd with your NID; set division/district/thana (decides your BRTA circle).

steps.title: Apply for learner licence
steps.detail: Upload photo, medical certificate, NID, utility bill, education certificate; pay Tk 518 (1 category) or Tk 748 (2 categories) online; print learner licence immediately.

steps.title: Practise and sit the test
steps.detail: On the scheduled date: biometrics, then written, oral and field test. BikeBD reports test dates are usually 3-6 months out (sometimes earlier).

steps.title: Apply for smart card
steps.detail: Upload learner licence with pass seal, pay Tk 4,497 (non-professional, 10 yr) or Tk 2,772 (professional, 5 yr) + Tk 60 postage online. Bank-counter payment is no longer accepted.

steps.title: Ride on temporary authorisation
steps.detail: After approval print the auto-generated Temporary Authorization slip from BSP and carry it (laminated) until the card arrives.

steps.title: Receive smart card by post
steps.detail: Delivered to your address; BikeBD reports processing usually takes 3-4 months. Police verification currently not required.

licence.typicalTimeline: Roughly 4-9 months end to end (2-3 months practice/test wait + 3-4 months card printing); temporary authorisation lets you ride legally meanwhile.
licence.statutoryBaseFees: Underlying gazette fees (Road Transport Rules 2022): learner Tk 250, competency test Tk 200 per attempt, licence issue Tk 300, annual licence fee Tk 300; BRTA's published totals above include these plus VAT/card charges.

ccPolicy.currentRule: Registration: BRTA registers motorcycles up to 375cc only if manufactured/assembled in Bangladesh (Road Transport & Highways Division decision, Oct 2023). Fully built (CBU) imports: every motorcycle above 165cc is banned from import under the Import Policy Order 2026-2029 (police excepted). Registered local manufacturers may import machinery and parts to build bikes up to 500cc.

history.rule: Import Policy Order 2026-2029 issued (SRO 308, valid to 31 Dec 2029). The gazette keeps the ban: import of all motorcycles above 165cc is prohibited, except for the police; registered motorcycle makers may import machinery and parts to build up to 500cc (Annex 1 part A item 8). The draft had proposed 375cc and an early Dhaka Times report said 375cc was allowed, but the final text does not say that. The amended text (updated to 24 Sep 2026) has the same clause.

insurance.summary: Third-party motor insurance was compulsory under the Motor Vehicles Ordinance 1983 but became optional under the Road Transport Act 2018 (in effect from Nov 2019; abolished in practice Dec 2020). In Mar 2024 the cabinet approved in principle an amendment to make it compulsory again with a fine up to Tk 3,000; it is cabinet-approved, not enacted, so cover is still optional. IDRA relaunched third-party cover as 'Motor Liability Insurance' on a one-year pilot from Aug 2025. We could not confirm whether the pilot continued after Aug 2026 (checked 14 Oct 2026): ask an insurer whether the policy is still sold and at what price.

laws.title: Helmet mandatory for rider and pillion
laws.detail: Road Transport Act 2018 requires the rider and passenger to wear a proper helmet. Riding without a helmet or carrying more than one pillion: fine up to Tk 10,000 or up to 3 months jail or both (plus demerit points).

laws.title: Maximum one pillion
laws.detail: Carrying more than two people (rider + one) is an offence with the same Tk 10,000 / 3-month penalty.

sources.title: Penalties for violating rules under the new Road Transport Act

laws.title: 'No helmet, no fuel'
laws.detail: Announced nationwide by the Road Transport minister on 15 May 2024: riders and pillions without helmets are to be refused fuel at pumps. Enforcement varies by area.

sources.title: Bikers without helmet will not get fuel

laws.title: BSTI helmet standard
laws.detail: BSTI standard BDS 1136:2022 covers motorcycle helmets, but the law only says 'proper' helmet and (per TBS) BSTI lacked a testing lab, so a BSTI-certified helmet is not strictly enforced. Buy a certified (BSTI/DOT/ECE) full- or open-face helmet anyway.

laws.title: Key penalties to know
laws.detail: Riding without a licence: Tk 25,000 or 6 months or both. Unregistered bike / no number plate: Tk 50,000 or 6 months or both. Illegal modifications (exhaust, brakes etc.): 1 to 3 years in jail, up to Tk 3 lakh, or both, and not bailable (s.84). Wrong-way riding: Tk 10,000 / 3 months.

laws.title: Ride-sharing on motorcycles
laws.detail: Governed by Ride-Sharing Service Guideline 2017 (in force 8 Mar 2018): only personal vehicles can be enlisted and must have up-to-date papers; from 2019 bikes ridden for Dhaka ride-sharing must be registered in Dhaka metro. Commercial riding generally needs a professional licence.

laws.title: No phone while riding
laws.detail: Using a mobile phone or similar device while riding is banned (s.49(1)). Penalty under s.92(2): up to 1 month in jail, a fine up to Tk 5,000, or both, plus 1 demerit point.

sources.title: Road Transport Act 2018 (official Bangla text)

laws.title: 12 demerit points on your licence
laws.detail: Every driving licence except a learner licence starts with 12 points (s.11). The Act lists speeding, jumping a red light, illegal overtaking and drunk or reckless driving among offences that cost points; phone use (s.92(2)) and failing to report a crash (s.95) cost 1 point each. The Act leaves the point level that triggers suspension or cancellation to the Rules.

sources.title: Road Transport Act 2018 (official Bangla text)

laws.title: After a crash: report it and get help
laws.detail: The rider must immediately tell the nearest police station (and the fire service or a hospital if needed) and get injured people to the nearest hospital as fast as possible (s.62(1)). Not doing so: up to 1 month in jail, a fine up to Tk 20,000, or both, plus 1 point (s.95). Call 999, the free national emergency line for police, fire service and ambulance.

sources.title: Road Transport Act 2018 (official Bangla text)
National emergency service 999 now fully operational

laws.title: If police stop you
laws.detail: For offences such as helmet, phone, plate or illegal-modification cases, a sub-inspector or sergeant (or higher) writes a charge and must give you a copy to sign or thumbprint; a fine paid by the date on it closes the case (s.108). In areas BRTA has notified, the officer may fine you on the spot but must record it on the set form and give you a receipt (s.113). Refusing the copy can lead to arrest without a warrant and an extra fine up to Tk 5,000 (s.108(4)). If your licence is taken you get a temporary receipt that lets you keep riding until its date (s.111). A bike held for an unpaid on-the-spot fine is released once you pay (s.113); for a bike sent to a dumping yard by a mobile court, apply to the court within 2 months (s.115).

sources.title: Road Transport Act 2018 (official Bangla text)

laws.title: Number plate, RFID tag and the front plate
laws.detail: Riding without the registration plate fixed and displayed breaks s.16(3): up to 6 months in jail, a fine up to Tk 50,000, or both (s.72). BRTA says the retro-reflective plate and RFID tag are mandatory, and on 24 Jun 2026 warned owners who had not collected them from their circle office of legal action (no deadline given). A front plate for motorcycles, so Dhaka's AI cameras can read it, was decided on 18 Jul 2026; a BRTA committee formed on 13 Aug 2026 was still working out size and position (report of 20 Aug 2026). Wait for BRTA's specification before fitting one.

sources.title: Road Transport Act 2018 (official Bangla text)
BRTA: retro-reflective number plate and RFID tag mandatory (Bangla)

lawsNote.text: Penalties are the maximums in the Road Transport Act 2018 as in force; courts and officers can impose less. Section numbers were checked against the official text on 14 Oct 2026. The 2024 amendment bill is cabinet-approved, not enacted, so it is not reflected here. General information, not legal advice.

items.title: Pedal e-bikes: no BRTA registration
items.detail: The government's 2023 electric-vehicle registration policy exempts e-bikes that can also be pedalled from BRTA registration, as reported when Walton launched its pedal e-bike (Feb 2023). Ask the dealer to confirm a model's status in writing.

sources.title: Walton launches affordable e-bike

items.title: Electric scooters and motorcycles: registered by motor power
items.detail: E-bikes without pedals are registered like any motorcycle, but the fee slab follows the motor's rated power: up to 5 kW pays the same Tk 2,000 registration fee as an up-to-100cc bike, above 5 kW pays Tk 3,000 (Road Transport Rules 2022, Schedule 1).

sources.title: BRTA - Road Transport Rules 2022, Schedule-1 fees (Bangladesh Gazette Extraordinary, 27 Dec 2022), via brta.gov.bd 'বিভিন্ন ফি'

items.title: VAT on e-bikes: 5% until June 2030
items.detail: The FY26 budget (June 2025) cut all VAT on e-bikes to 5% until June 2030, alongside duty cuts for makers of key parts; customs duty on e-bikes was still 26-60% depending on the components (Daily Star, 13 Jun 2025). We have not checked whether the FY27 budget changed this.

usedChecklist.title: Match the blue book / DRC to the seller
usedChecklist.detail: The name on the Registration Certificate (old blue book) or Digital Registration Certificate must match the seller's NID. If not, the seller isn't the legal owner - insist on transfer from the registered owner.

usedChecklist.title: Check chassis and engine numbers
usedChecklist.detail: Compare the chassis (frame) number stamped on the steering head and the engine number on the crankcase with the DRC. Look for re-stamping, grinding marks, fresh paint or welding around the numbers.

usedChecklist.title: Verify registration and dues online
usedChecklist.detail: Use the BRTA Service Portal (bsp.brta.gov.bd) dues/fees lookup by registration number to confirm the bike exists in BRTA records and see unpaid tax-token/fees. Match the RFID number plate to the DRC.

usedChecklist.title: Tax token validity
usedChecklist.detail: Check the tax token expiry. Unpaid years plus the one-time Tk 1,150 Financial Assistance Fund (if not paid) will become your bill. Bikes that completed 10 years of road tax only need a Tk 23 'tax-free' token every 5 years.

usedChecklist.title: Loan / hire-purchase clearance
usedChecklist.detail: If the DRC shows a bank/leasing hire-purchase entry, get the lender's loan-clearance letter; BRTA won't transfer without it (hire-purchase removal fee Tk 1,000 per 2022 rules).

usedChecklist.title: Ownership transfer at BRTA
usedChecklist.detail: Seller signs TTO form and sales receipt (Tk 10 revenue stamp) and a sale affidavit with photo; buyer signs TO + TTO forms, a buyer affidavit on non-judicial stamp (BikeBD: Tk 300), specimen signature form with 3 stamp photos; attach original DRC/blue book and both NIDs; pay fee and apply via BSP. BikeBD's (older, 2014-based) figure is Tk 2,665 if already on digital registration; confirm current fee on BSP before paying.

usedChecklist.title: Accident damage signs
usedChecklist.detail: Look for bent/re-welded frame, misaligned handlebar vs front wheel, uneven fork tubes or oil leaks from fork seals, scraped bar ends/levers/footpegs, mismatched or new paint on only some panels, and pulling to one side on a straight test ride.

usedChecklist.title: Flood / water damage signs
usedChecklist.detail: Check for silt or rust inside the headlight, tail lamp, under the seat and in switch housings; corroded wiring connectors; milky engine oil; rust on fasteners that should be clean. Dhaka monsoon waterlogging makes this common.

usedChecklist.title: Odometer tampering
usedChecklist.detail: Compare odometer to wear: worn footpeg rubbers, seat foam, grips, chain/sprocket condition, brake disc lip. Ask for service-centre records (authorised service centres log km). Digital clusters can also be reset.

usedChecklist.title: Mechanical test ride
usedChecklist.detail: Cold start, idle stability, smoke colour, clutch slip, gear engagement, brake feel and ABS (if fitted), electrical items. Ride long enough to warm up.

usedChecklist.title: Legal ride-away
usedChecklist.detail: Don't ride the bike until the transfer is filed in your name and you hold a valid licence; carry DRC, tax token and licence (or temporary authorisation).

usedChecklist.title: Transfer online, with the seller present
usedChecklist.detail: Under a BRTA notice of 1 Sep 2026, buyer and seller apply for the transfer at bsp.brta.gov.bd, then the seller's fingerprint is checked on a handheld biometric device; BRTA says the transfer can finish the same day. You can give your own biometrics for the new digital registration certificate. The Act (s.21) requires the transfer after a sale, so agree before paying in full that the seller will come for the biometric check.

usedChecklist.title: Read the VIN prefix
usedChecklist.detail: The first three characters of the chassis number (VIN) name the maker, for example ME1 India Yamaha, MD2 Bajaj (also Bajaj-built KTMs), MD6 TVS, ME4 Honda Motorcycle and Scooter India, MBL Hero MotoCorp and MB8 Suzuki Motorcycle India. A prefix that does not fit the brand, or a VIN that differs from the DRC, is a reason to walk away.

usedChecklist.title: Yamaha FZS: which generation is it?
usedChecklist.detail: The V3 has the key on the fuel tank, an LED headlight, front-wheel ABS and a sealed chain, and weighs about 5 kg more than the V2 (BikeBD). The V4, launched in Bangladesh on 28 Sep 2024, adds traction control, position lamps in the headlight and a Bluetooth link to Yamaha's Connect app (ACI). An FZS without ABS sold as a V3 or V4 is mislabelled.

usedChecklist.title: Suzuki Gixxer: old or 2019 shape?
usedChecklist.detail: Rancon launched the 2019-generation Gixxer and Gixxer SF in Bangladesh on 1 Jul 2020. The newer Gixxer has a flat LED headlight (the old one was halogen), split rider and pillion seats and a taller seat; the newer SF is styled like the SF 250 and also has an LED headlight. Each came as carburettor + disc or fuel injection + ABS, so check for both before paying the FI price.
